text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move that has seen the Big Australian lose A$750 million over 11 years, BHP has finally quit its 36.5 per cent stake in the Foster's Brewing Group. The A$1.78 billion exit by BHP has been followed by the departure of 13 per cent stakeholder Asahi Brweries, who will offload its stake in a A$625 million share buyback scheme. Page 1.

In a move that may signal an exit from the thermal coal market, BHP Coal Ltd is planning to quit its A$185 million flagship investment, the Mount Owen open cut mine in the Hunter Valley. The decision to sell after only eight months of involvement shows BP's new hard-nosed review of its assets. Page 33.

After last year being appointed managing director of News Corp, Lachlan Murdoch has now been appointed chairman of the global media group's Australian arm, News Limited. The move completes the withdrawal of outgoing chairman Ken Cowley from the day-to-day operations of the company. Page 33.

James Hardie Industries Ltd managing director Dr Keith Barton revealed yesterday the company's earnings from its Australian operations had shrunk because of the punishing slump in the local housing and construction industry. The building products group sid operating profits fell 12 per cent to A$51.3 million. Page 34.

In a move that would create Australia's largest defence industry conglomerate with annual turnover close to A$1 billion, Transfield Defence Systems (TDS) is considering a merger with the Australian Submarine Corporation (ASC). TDS chief executive Andrew Johnson said discussions are taking place. Page 34.

Under new arrangements with its departing parent company ICI plc , ICI Australia will be free to develop its own paint markets in Asia and will take full control of the development of explosive markets in China and Indonesia. ICI plc group strategic plannng manager Rob Milligan said the moves will open up competition between the two groups. Page 34.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a deal that will see the two main shareholders in the Foster's Brewing Group, BHP and Asahi, sell their holdings, Foster's chief executive Ted Kunkel has announced a A$625 million buyback of most of Asahi's 13.8 per cent share, and a A$1.54 billion plcement of the lion's share of BHP's 36.5 per cent stake. Page 25.

While BHP's shares fell 14 cents to A$18.83 on the back of the Foster's deal, BHP analysts believe the sale of the first trenches of shares, which represents 31.4 per cent of its 36.5 per cent stake in Foster's, for A$2.40 each was a positive result for te company, which could now leave the way open for internal reform. Page 25.

Pasminco, the world's largest zinc and lead refiner, has lined up a syndicate of banks to arrange a A$795 million debt facility for the A$1.4 billion purchase and development of the Century zinc deposit in northern Queensland. The company will also go onthe markets to raise a further A$600 million in equity. Page 27.

New Zealand based Fletcher Challenge has informed the Foreign Investment Review Board it is planning to buy out News Limited's 50 per cent of Australian Newsprint Mills. ANM supplies about 70 per cent of Australia's newsprint. Fletcher, which already ows half of ANM, is believed to be close to signing a deal worth A$250 million for News Limited's stake. Page 27.

The magazine arm of News Corporation, PMP Communications, yesterday flagged an earnings drop of up to 20 per cent this financial year due to soft retail sales, a sluggish economy, and lower advertising sales. PMP shares fell by 16c to close at A$3.40. Pag 27.

Visy Industries has upgraded the size of its proposed pulp mill in southern NSW to a A$300 million investment and is expected to decide if the project will proceed by the end of the year. Special "enabling legislation" now under consideration by the NSW government would give the project resource security by guaranteeing a supply of plantation timber from NSW State Forests for at least 30 years. Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In the biggest share placement in Australian history, JB Were and ABN Amro Rothschild were confident all 616 million shares in the Foster's Brewing Group - a 31.5 per cent share - would be sold by this afternoon. The success of the A$1.5 billion deal depnds on the interest of Australian and overseas institutional investors. Page 25.

The sharemarket was affected by rumours that the Westpac Banking Corporation's A$1.4 billion bid for the Bank of Melbourne would not be approved by authorities, with the share price of the Bank of Melbourne slumping 4 per cent, and Westpac lifting 3.6 percent. Page 25.

After posting a 7.3 per cent rise in net profit to A$10.1 million for the year to March, television production and distribution company Southern Star has indicated further expansion overseas. Chairman Neil Balnaves said the company would concentrate on icreasing the business in the United Kingdom, Canada and China. Page 27.

There was speculation on the market yesterday that Microsoft's Internet content division, the Microsoft Network, will merge with the newly formed online division of PBL, a move that would combine the fledgling media operations of Microsoft together with te media operations of Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd. Page 27.

Whitegoods and building products group Email chairman Peter Cottrell says company trading has fallen off since the end of March. His comments came as Email posted a flat net profit of A$55 million for the twelve months to March. Page 27.

At a meeting in Melbourne yesterday, Ansett Australia executive chairman Rod Eddington has asked unions to accept a six month delay to agreed pay rises as the company moves on plans to return the airline to profitability. Ansett has asked unions to stall a 2 per cent wage rise due in September 1997 to March 1998. Page 27.
THE AGE

Brokers believe local institutions will take up over half of the A$1,534 million, 31.5 per cent block of Foster's Brewing Group shares after BHP sold its share of the company yesterday. The share placement will be the biggest in Australian history and chif executive Ted Kunkel said he believes it is a great opportunity for Foster's and its shareholders. Page B1.

Foster's Brewing Group chief executive Ted Kunkel sidestepped questions on the colourful past of the brewer, instead saying he was looking forward to committing himself to improving shareholder value rather than addressing uncertainty over an overhang of oster's shares. Page B1.

Ansett Airlines, which last year slumped to a loss of A$18.5 million, yesterday asked its 18,000 employees and union leaders to put off an agreed 8 per cent pay rise, which would come in four 2 per cent increments. Under the airline's proposal, the first two increments would be put off by six months. Page B1.

The A$1.5 billion exit from the Foster's Brewing Group by BHP will deliver BHP new fire-power to its balance sheet. However, it is not expected the group will take up any new big acquisitions, given that it is currently reviewing its asset performance. Page B2.

James Hardie Industries reported a dismal outlook for its Australian operation in its annual results released yesterday. The building products group will rely on its United States operations for earnings growth. James Hardie managing director Keith Barton forecast demand for Australian housing over the next three years would remain below that in 1993-95 after the group posted a 12.3 per cent fall in net profit before abnormals to A$51.3 million for the year to March 31, and a bottom line of A$83 million fter abnormal profits from selling operations had been taken into account. Page B3.

The producer of Water Rats and Blue Heelers, Southern Star, recorded a net profit for the year to March of $10.1 million, a 7 per cent increase on its prospectus forecast of A$9.4 million. The company declared a final dividend of 3c, franked to 1.4c. It said it did not expect future dividends would be fully franked. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
